title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act s. 28 — Statutory provision (ACA s. 28)

content.overview: Section 28 distinguishes international commercial arbitration seated in India from other arbitrations. In international commercial arbitration, parties may designate the substantive law; absent such designation, the tribunal applies the rules of law it considers appropriate. In other arbitrations, the tribunal applies the substantive law for the time being in force in India. The tribunal decides in accordance with the contract and applicable trade usages.

content.study:
Section 28 — Rules applicable to substance of dispute

Section 28 distinguishes international commercial arbitration seated in India from other arbitrations. In international commercial arbitration, parties may designate the substantive law; absent such designation, the tribunal applies the rules of law it considers appropriate. In other arbitrations, the tribunal applies the substantive law for the time being in force in India. The tribunal decides in accordance with the contract and applicable trade usages.

The provision must be applied by identifying its operative conditions, the procedural stage and its connected sections. Statutory exceptions and party agreements must be kept distinct from the default rule.
